newsitem.title: IRAN: Kohl tells Tehran charges not meant to offend-Iran.
newsitem.headline: Kohl tells Tehran charges not meant to offend-Iran.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl assured Iran in a message on Thursday that terrorism charges by a German prosecutor against Tehran leaders were not meant to offend, Iranian state television said.

"Helmut Kohl, in an important message to the President (Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani) stressed that the German government and the judicial body of that country has meant no offense to the Iranian people's religious feelings and to Iran's religious leaders," the television said.

Relations between Iran and main trading partner Germany are strained over the prosecutor's charge last week that Iranian spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and other Tehran officials ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator at a Berlin restaurant in 1992.

"In the past few days I have been witnessing with worry and concern the trend in relations between the two states, especially its reflection in the press. With such a trend, it is unfortunately possible that the long-term and friendly bilateral ties will suffer," the television quoted Kohl as saying.
Kohl assured Rafsanjani that German courts were independent and did not pursue a political goal, it said.
Iranian media and officials have denounced the charges as an affront to Islamic beliefs and religious leaders and some have demanded that Germany should apologise.
Germany's ambassador to Tehran delivered the letter to Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Morteza Sarmadi at the foreign ministry on Thursday evening, the television said.
"He (Kohl)...stressed that it was in the two nations' interests to avoid tension in bilateral ties," it said.
"I have always been committed to confidence-building dialogue between the two great world religions Islam and Christianity," Kohl was quoted by the television as saying.
Tehran radio earlier said crowds chanting "Death to world arrogance (West)" and "Death to America" marched in several Iranian towns and cities on Thursday to protest against the German charges.
German officials have condemned as death threats calls raised at some of the demonstrations in the past few days that the prosecutor should be "executed".
Tehran officially protested last week to Bonn over the charges. German prosecutors have demanded life sentences for an Iranian and a Lebanese who were tried for the killings.
